stem:
A varying current *I* passes through a resistor of resistance *R* in the circuit shown in Fig. 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Fig. 7.2 shows the variation with time *t* of *I*.

[[fig:f2]]

The current has magnitude 2*I*₀ when it is in the positive direction and *I*₀ when it is in the negative direction. The period of the variation of the current is *T*.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead: Determine expressions, in terms of *I*₀ and *R*, for the power *P* dissipated in the resistor for the times when:
parts.text: the current is in the negative direction

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the current is in the positive direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.3, sketch the variation of *P* with *t* between *t* = 0 and *t* = 2.0*T*. Label the power axis with an appropriate scale.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Use your answer in (b) to determine an expression, in terms of *I*₀ and *R*, for:
parts.text: the mean power ⟨*P*⟩ in the resistor

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current *I*ᵣ.ₘ.ₛ. in the resistor.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A circuit with a resistor labelled R in the lower wire, an open gap in the upper wire, and a downward current arrow labelled I on the left.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A current-versus-time graph from 0 to 2.0T, with the current alternating between −I₀ and 2I₀.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.3
figures.alt: A blank gridded graph with power P on the vertical axis and time t marked from 0 to 2.0T on the horizontal axis.
